stem: Which paediatric fracture presentation should be referred early?

options.text: An undisplaced fracture being supported in a sling
A stable incomplete fracture without other concerns
A fracture already immobilised with dry plaster
A distal injury placed in an appropriate back-slab

explanation: An open fracture should be referred early because it carries a higher risk of contamination and complications and needs urgent specialist assessment.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because open fractures require early referral for urgent assessment, treatment, and infection prevention.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a simple undisplaced fracture in a sling is not, by itself, an automatic reason for early referral.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a stable incomplete fracture without other concerns is generally low risk and does not need early referral on its own.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a fracture already immobilised in dry plaster is not the specific early-referral warning in this question.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because appropriate back-slab immobilisation is a management step, not an indication for early referral on its own.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
